core_obligations: Set up the framework lemma: its assumptions (1) and (2) follow from the cited locality lemma for affine morphisms (proof lines 1776-1781).

Construct the descent datum \varphi : X' \times_Z Z' \to Z' \times_Z X' (both sides represent Z' \times_Z Z' \times_Z X), note it is a descent datum for X'/Z'/Z, and invoke effectivity of affine descent to get an affine Y \to Z with \psi : Z' \times_Z Y \to X' compatible with the descent data (proof lines 1783-1800).

Interpret \psi as an element of \check{H}^0(\mathcal{Y}, X) for the fpqc covering \mathcal{Y} = {Z' \times_Z Y \to Y}, use the fpqc sheaf condition for X to obtain Y \to X, and conclude via isomorphism descent that X is representable by an affine scheme (proof lines 1800-1815).
proof_roadmap: Feed the two locality assumptions into the framework lemma.
Build the descent datum and descend it effectively to an affine scheme.
Glue the descended scheme to X through the fpqc sheaf condition and descend the isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The proof works through the framework lemma for descending properties of morphisms: its assumptions (1) and (2) hold by the cited locality lemma for affineness; then for a surjective flat Z' \to Z of affines with the base change f' affine, it builds the canonical descent datum \varphi : X' \times_Z Z' \to Z' \times_Z X' from representability, invokes effectivity of affine descent (cited), obtains an affine Y \to Z, and uses the fpqc sheaf condition for X (cited proposition) to turn \psi \in \check{H}^0(\mathcal{Y}, X) into a morphism Y \to X whose base change to Z' is an isomorphism, concluding representability of X by an affine scheme via isomorphism descent. The descent-datum construction and the sheaf-condition step are the substance.
